sections.h2: How do I reach the Mecosta County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Documents for recording can be mailed or shipped by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307, and the office phone is (231) 592-0148. Big Rapids is the county seat. Call before you travel to confirm recording hours.

The register of deeds records and maintains the real estate records for every parcel in Mecosta County. Records are indexed in full back to January 1, 1968, and all documents back to 1859 are imaged and tagged by liber and page. Searches run through two portals, Countyfusion and the Vanguard public search site.

The office also takes passport applications, with its own hours and a separate $35 acceptance fee that has no bearing on a house sale.

sections.h2: What is Mecosta County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Mecosta County covers 571 square miles, of which 555 are land, and it holds more than 100 lakes, rivers and streams. The Muskegon River runs through Big Rapids, and Ferris State University sits in the county seat. County government was organized in 1859, and the county includes 16 townships, four villages (Barryton, Mecosta, Morley and Stanwood) and the city of Big Rapids.

The Census Bureau estimated 42,320 residents on July 1, 2025, a 4.9 percent rise over the April 2020 base. The county counted 21,490 housing units, and 76.9 percent of homes were owner-occupied in 2020 to 2024. The median home value was $178,900, below the figures for Marquette and Mason counties.

Whether the parcel sits in Big Rapids, a village or one of the townships, the deed is recorded in Big Rapids, but assessing and tax collection happen locally. Confirm the parcel's local unit before you request a payoff or a tax certificate.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost at the Mecosta County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or similar instrument costs $30.00. The county notes this includes the fee under MCL 600.2567a and the $5.00 automation fee. If one document assigns or discharges several instruments, add $3.00 for each extra one.

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings go to the Secretary of State.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Mecosta County sale?
sections.html:
The county rate is 55 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, and the state rate is $3.75 for each $500. Both apply when the value is $100 or more. The state rate is set by MCL 207.525, and the seller is the liable party under MCL 207.523.

On a house selling for $175,000 there are 350 units of $500. That gives $1,312.50 in state tax and $192.50 in county tax, or $1,505.00 in all. The Register of Deeds office collects both taxes with the recording fee, and the state act requires payment within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

The deed must show the total value of the real property, or a real estate valuation affidavit must be attached and the deed must say so. The office charges nothing to file the affidavit. Exemptions have to be stated on the instrument itself, and MCL 207.526 lists them. A deed from a parent to a child and a transfer made in lieu of foreclosure are two common examples.

sections.h2: What documents does Mecosta County reject at recording?
sections.html:
The county publishes an eleven-point checklist drawn from Michigan statutes. The items that trip up most sellers are these:

  • Names typed or printed under each signature that differ from the notary acknowledgment
  • No grantee address, or no name and address for the drafter
  • A notary block missing the commission expiration date
  • A deed for a surviving owner, with no certified death certificate recorded
  • A court order that is not certified and sealed by the clerk of the court
  • Text smaller than 10 point, or a margin smaller than 2 1/2 inches on the first page
  • A first line that names more than one recordable event
  • No statement of the total value of the real estate and no affidavit

Paper must be white, 20-pound, and between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches. A closing agent can check each item before the deed is sent.

sections.h2: Is a tax certificate needed to record a Mecosta County deed?
sections.html:
It is needed on warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant of warranty, land contracts and assignments of land contracts. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and confirms that taxes are paid for the five years before the instrument date (MCL 211.135). Quitclaim deeds with no warranty clause are excused.

The Mecosta County Treasurer passes delinquent bills to foreclosure after a set timeline, so a seller with old taxes should ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing. The companion property tax guide for this county covers the summer and winter due dates, the delinquency schedule and the appeal calendar.

sections.h2: Where do I search Mecosta County land records online?
sections.html:
Two public portals are linked from the county page: Countyfusion and the Vanguard public search at mecosta.mi.publicsearch.us. The county lists a support line for the Vanguard site, (888) 608-1808. Index books, including oil and gas books, are imaged on the Countyfusion site.

The land records portal and the map viewer sit on the Equalization page, along with the township tax maps for Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Matching the parcel number on the map to the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before a closing.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Mecosta County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30.00 per instrument. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each extra one. Copies cost $1.00 per page.

faqs.q: What is the Mecosta County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state charges $3.75 per $500 of value and the county charges 55 cents per $500. A $175,000 sale produces $1,505.00 combined. The seller is liable unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Where do I send a deed for recording in Mecosta County?
faqs.a: Mail or ship it to the Register of Deeds at 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Call (231) 592-0148 first to confirm the paperwork, the fee and the payment method the office accepts.

faqs.q: Does Mecosta County accept court documents that are not certified?
faqs.a: No. A court order must be certified and sealed by the clerk of the court before the register of deeds will record it. A plain copy of the order will be returned.

faqs.q: How far back are Mecosta County records indexed?
faqs.a: Records are fully indexed back to January 1, 1968, and documents dating to 1859 are imaged by liber and page. Both the Countyfusion and Vanguard portals are listed on the county page.
